The latter is an issue in internal guns, which can cause the tungsten emitter to short circuit via an arc event. This type of failure can cause significant damage to the welder as well as part being welded; however, with proper preventative maintenance and a skilled operator and engineering team, this can be avoided. The higher voltage gun is able to generate much deeper weld penetration than the low voltage gun, but both are able to fabricate all welds needed in a copper accelerator. High voltage welders are generally more expensive than low voltage systems because of the increase power supply costs, more complex electrical isolation needs within the gun as well as thicker- chamber walls to shield process-generated x-rays. A high power, high voltage gun can be used for complex beam manipulation which Page 23 of 55 “Manufacturing full-scale high gradient copper accelerators: Electron beam welding and allied processes” Prepared for the U.S. Department of Energy ARDAP program has been shown to reduce porosity defects, but further research will be needed for implantation of this type of advanced control system in copper accelerator manufacturing. Beam Deflection Single spot beam deflection is commonly used in electron beam welding to increase the size of the weld pool as shown in Figure 19. The circular deflection pattern is often used to bridge gaps when fit-up of components is not ideal. More complex deflection patterns can be used to control fluid flow, melt pool geometry, cracking and penetration. It should be noted that these patterns generally come preloaded on the machine from manufacturers and little to no research has been performed on the effect of the different patters, the size of the patterns, or the speed of deflection on the melt pool and solidified microstructure. A cosmetic post penetration weld pass could also be completed by performing a second revolution with a parameter set designed to smooth out the weld surface. Multi-process technology shown in Figure 21 is similar to the multi-pool technology with the preheat leading the weld on both sides. Having preheat leading the weld, or on the sides of the weld could control the defect formation such as cracking, or slow down cooling time of the weld pool to enable the escape of trapped gas and thus limit porosity.
